claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks proper tutorials and clear instructions, leaving players without guidance on what to do initially.

⭐☆☆☆☆ 

Playing Stranded Deep especially in co-op feels like the game is actively trying to punish the players.

There is basically no proper tutorial, so you're thrown onto an island with no idea what you're supposed to do. You get poisoned five minutes into the game, but the antidote requires a crafting level you obviously don't have yet. Good luck figuring that out.

The crafting system is unnecessarily confusing, resources are limited at the beginning, and the game explains almost nothing. We spent half our time Googling how to do basic things that should have been explained in the game.

Then there's the multiplayer. If both players die, instead of simply respawning or reloading the save, you're thrown back into the lobby. Then, every single time you try to join again, you have to sit there for five minutes waiting for the world to sync.

And don't even get me started on trying to interact with objects. You find useful raft parts underwater, but the game barely tells you how to move or use them.

The survival concept is genuinely fun, and exploring islands and shipwrecks can be exciting, but the terrible lack of explanation, confusing mechanics, clunky controls, and painfully slow co-op syncing make the experience incredibly frustrating.

This game doesn't feel challenging because survival is difficult. It feels challenging because you're constantly fighting the game's terrible design.

Would I recommend it? Absolutely not unless you have unlimited patience.

Absolutely terrible multiplayer experience

I tried this game in single player first, where you at least get some basic tutorial steps explaining what you're supposed to do. Because of that, I convinced my friend to buy the game so we could play together.

What a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mistake.

The moment we started multiplayer, the tutorial was completely gone. We were thrown onto an island with basically zero guidance, struggling to figure out what resources we needed and where to find them. Even worse, some resources don't seem to respawn, making the early game even more frustrating when you don't know what you're doing.

And then there's the crafting system, which is honestly bizarre.

You have crafting stations, but apparently you're not actually supposed to craft things inside the stations. Instead, you just have to stand somewhere near them, open the regular crafting menu, and craft the item from there.

What is the point of having a crafting station then?

Coming from other survival games, this feels unnecessarily unintuitive and backwards. You would expect to interact with the crafting station and see what can be produced there. Instead, you're just standing around it while using a completely separate crafting menu. It's not difficult — it's just stupidly designed and confusing when you're first learning the game.

Then there are the technical issues:

3–4 minute loading times just to start/open the multiplayer game.
Trees and other objects sometimes don't load until you're practically standing next to them.
We both died, and instead of simply letting us continue, the game automatically closed the session and sent us back to the main menu.
We then had to reopen the multiplayer game and load the save again, taking roughly 5 minutes just to get back into the game after dying.

This is not how a multiplayer survival game should work.

PROS:
The game looks decent
Music is great
Early game is fun

CONS:
All kinds of janky
Items will disappear for no reason 
No consistency where inventory will go when you craft something
No animations when animals attack you, they just kind of run into you
No depth. We are 15 hours into a file day 11 and it feels like there is nothing to do.
Islands all very small and generic
Too far between Island to explore and not a lot of items in starting zone
Poor skill progression. If you get poisoned early your game is just done
Mid and I assume late game are just boring with no objectives

NOTE: I have posted my specs for my pc below and for some reason this game even on Low settings was just throtling my rig yet when my wife was playing on the Steam Deck in docked mode it looked worse (obviously) but performed better

Conclusion: There are dozens of better survival games on Steam for the same price or cheaper. Save your money on this one.

Me and my friend have been making excellent progress, then inventory disappears, the raft we spent 2 hours creating launched into the air and spiraled in circles until it reached outer space. It was funny! But what wasn't funny that we couldn't get it back and we were stranded on an island with nothing left gg's.

Honestly, this was a terrible experience.

My friend and I bought this game tonight because we wanted to try a survival game we hadn’t played before and just have some fun. Instead, in the few hours we played, we spent more time disconnecting, reconnecting, and waiting for the world to sync than actually playing.

The multiplayer felt extremely unstable. Whenever one of us died, there was a good chance the other person would get disconnected. Items would randomly disappear. At one point, we got knocked off the raft in an area with more visual effects, and both of us disconnected again. Then it was back to waiting for the world to sync.

Even getting into the game was inconsistent. The first time my friend tried to join me, he couldn’t connect at all, so we tried the reverse and only then did it work.

Overall, it was a very frustrating experience. The game might have potential, but the constant disconnects, syncing issues, and lost items made it feel almost unplayable in co-op. I really wanted to enjoy it, but based on tonight’s experience, I can’t recommend it.

I dont know where to start with this review. My wife follows some social media person who plays this game and wanted to try it out so i bought copies for both of us..... as someone who plays a lot of survivval games i would have to say this is on the low end of this genre for quality.

The game looks decent
Music is great

All kinds of janky

No depth. We are 15 hours into a file day 11 and it feels like there is nothing to do.
Islands all very small and generic
Too far between Island to explore and not a lot of items in starting zone
Poor skill progression. If you get poisoned early your game is just done
Mid and I assume late game are just boring with no objectives

Conclusion: There are dozens of better survival games on Steam for the same price or cheaper. Save your money on this one.

claims.claim: Reviewers point out that online co-op lacks in-game text chat or voice communication features.

citations.review_text: So today I purchased this game ok. I seen we can play with friends online. Turns out there is no ingame text or voice like seriously! Yea developers nice way to advertise a game but then fail to leave out a very vital part! Game dynamics are ok. But already disappointed with the game because one of the most important parts of the game are left out.

⭐☆☆☆☆ 

Playing Stranded Deep especially in co-op feels like the game is actively trying to punish the players.

There is basically no proper tutorial, so you're thrown onto an island with no idea what you're supposed to do. You get poisoned five minutes into the game, but the antidote requires a crafting level you obviously don't have yet. Good luck figuring that out.

The crafting system is unnecessarily confusing, resources are limited at the beginning, and the game explains almost nothing. We spent half our time Googling how to do basic things that should have been explained in the game.

Then there's the multiplayer. If both players die, instead of simply respawning or reloading the save, you're thrown back into the lobby. Then, every single time you try to join again, you have to sit there for five minutes waiting for the world to sync.

And don't even get me started on trying to interact with objects. You find useful raft parts underwater, but the game barely tells you how to move or use them.

The survival concept is genuinely fun, and exploring islands and shipwrecks can be exciting, but the terrible lack of explanation, confusing mechanics, clunky controls, and painfully slow co-op syncing make the experience incredibly frustrating.

This game doesn't feel challenging because survival is difficult. It feels challenging because you're constantly fighting the game's terrible design.

Would I recommend it? Absolutely not unless you have unlimited patience.

The survival is ok, but listen... you cannot collect water when it rains! The only source of water is by distilling leaves and palm leaves.

The rest of the survival mechanics are easy and food is abundant!

THE ISLAND HORROR: The islands are small and repetitive, each island has the same script: sunken ships near by, crabs and boars inhabit the island. Its a copy paste of the same island and there are over 20 islands for you to "explore" and all of them look the same with same boring sunken ships and loot.

This game has so much potential. The vibes are amazing; I am excited for the sequel, but this game feels unfinished. It feels half-baked. There are so many game design decisions I see they made, and I wonder how they decided on them. You get "endgame" gear minutes into the game. It feels like there should be another tier of items later in the game. Why is navigation so terrible?

And the most damning decision: why in the world would you make a game that wants you to migrate around a huge map from island to island on a raft, but not allow you to place ANY items on the raft? The entire game, I am just trying to disassemble and reassemble my "house items" to bring them to new islands, and when you disassemble them, you lose some of their ingredients. If you want us to be migratory, at least allow us to disassemble them into placeable blueprints so it's less painful to move. Multiplayer is buggy, and WHY IS THE MAP OFF CENTER.

This game was released years after Raft and copied none of the great design decisions they made with that game. Just play Raft instead and try out the sequel for this game because there is potential here, but this iteration of the game is squandered.

Don`t buy this game. It`s one of those, which in theory is awesome, but the sheer amount of bugs and technical flaws destroy every little good thing left. absolute buggy mess.   maybe single player has a chance to be played to the end of the game but in multiplayer good luck.  people will tell you to store items in chests and remove things from just sitting on the islands but ultimately it is just a tiny bandaid trying to hold back a flood of unoptimized filth.  disconnects every few minutes, items missing, etc.   don't spend money on this absolute trash heap unless you really like spending most of your time trying to avoid bugs.

such a waste.

Beutiful & Vivid graphics yet basic & low GPU intensive. Object / land interactivity is boxy & basic but does not affect gameplay too much.
Audio is also done well with impending doom & placid relaxing modes.
Underwater exploration provides the fear of drowing (or shark attack) with somewhat realistic variance in visibility both underwater and above.
Crafting system is laid out instead of learned which has pro's & cons, bad for discovery but good for learning requirements.
Gameplay after 20 Hrs in game is becomming a bit repetitive with no clear story direction provided, but the 1st 10 were quite immersive and the 1st 20 were quite progressive. I expect the game is pushing exploration now with less pressure on survival.
No Map yet found and only landmarks and a compass to guide makes it easy to get turned around (touch of realism?).
It would be great to have some way of building a tall flagpost and/or small signposts to aid with direction of arrival etc, some buidling mechanincs permit rudamentory systems for this.
The Multiplayer is a big advantage to this game with limited resources on each island and gametime delay of respawn for critical ingredients means teamwork is required with delegation of duties.

However, the multiplayer is buggy, with random item dissapear, inventory clashes, inability to label crates etc, and most notably the extraordinary loading/syncing time, its like the game files need to be completely downloaded from your peer and can take 5-10min+ to reload (This sincerely needs fixing by developers, its quite a distraction from an otherwise impressive basic game).
Not quite as immersive and polished as Survival games like "Green Hell" (Its quite simiar), but better crafting than "The Forest". No solid way of building a house boat though or towing objects with the raft...
Good game but dont have high expectations, almost zero story. 3/5*.

[b]The Good:[/b]
* Perfect Castaway Vibe: Nails the slow, meditative solo survival loop.Rewarding 
* Progression: Starting with sticks and slowly building an epic island base and custom raft never gets old.Beautiful
